target_customer: Employers (HR, culture and inclusion leaders) paying for a confidential ombuds style platform for employees
problem: Employees hesitate to report bias, discrimination and harassment for fear of retaliation, and companies lack data on systemic issues.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with human ombuds style guidance and analytics
product_category: HR tech, workplace conduct and ombuds platform

founders.name: Lisa Gelobter
prior_employers: US Department of Education (Chief Digital Service Officer)
previous_startups: Shockwave (early internet technology, per YC bio)
founders.background_notes: Later became New York City Chief Technology Officer per a recent bio. Wikipedia dates founding to 2016, CB Insights to 2017.

competitors.name: Spot
competitors.what: AI chatbot tools for workplace harassment reporting and investigations
competitors.funding_then: Raised $500K in February 2018 per CB Insights

technical_complexity.rationale: A confidential reporting and analytics platform is standard software; the hard part was trust, privacy and professional ombuds delivery.

defensibility.rationale: Trust with employees and enterprise HR contracts helped, but the software was copyable and several reporting startups launched around 2018.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found; AllVoices and Culture Shift later became competitors.

market_need_then: The 2017 #MeToo movement created sudden corporate demand for harassment prevention and reporting tools.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven; tagline 'Work culture that works for everyone'.

branding.brand_signature: Capital EQ in the name, a play on equitable
branding.community_and_virality: Founder profiled by TheGrio, Devex and an EEOC testimony; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name signals the mission and the founder drew press and conference visibility, but the odd capitalization and the confusion with the word equitable (and unrelated Equitable Holdings in search) limit findability.

outcome_analysis: tEQuitable launched around the 2017 #MeToo moment with a well known founder and joined YC in Winter 2018. It remains active and now describes itself as a modern ombuds practice, but funding stayed small and sources disagree on how much was raised. Competitors such as AllVoices and Culture Shift grew in the same category, and no clear breakout or failure story is public.
notes: Funding conflicts and is unverified: CB Insights lists about $120K over three rounds (latest a convertible note in 2018-06, Ulu Ventures among investors), Wikipedia says more than $2M raised. Neither recorded as a round. The Crunchbase page held placeholder text. Competitor list is thin: Spot is the only entry with a date near the batch. Whether Gelobter still runs the company after becoming NYC CTO is not stated. Update: Wikipedia states more than 2M in venture capital raised, above the roughly 120K in CB Insights rounds; the gap is known but no dated round source was found, so no round is added (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Gelobter).
